'''Support abilities''' {{J|サポートアビリティ|Sapōto Abiriti}} are abilities that enhance a character. They are also called '''passive abilities''', '''job traits''', or '''auto-abilities'''. They range from providing bonuses to improving equipment options, [[stats|general stats]], physical or magical resists, and so on. Some support abilities are innate to a particular [[Job system|job]] or monster.

==Appearances==
===''[[Final Fantasy IV]]''===
{{Main|Augment (Final Fantasy IV)}}
There are no specific support abilities in the 2D versions, although equipment can provide effects akin to them. The Augment ability system is the support ability system for the 3D versions that allows characters to inherit and equip abilities from other characters.

===''[[Final Fantasy V]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy V support abilities}}
Support abilities are tied to [[Final Fantasy V jobs|jobs]], and many jobs have them as innate traits that they can learn via ABP so the become usable by other jobs. Some equipment also provide support effects, such as the 0[[Reflect Ring (Final Fantasy V)|Reflect Ring]] providing [[Auto-Reflect]].

===''[[Final Fantasy VI]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy VI support abilities}}
Support abilities are gained by equipping the appropriate [[Relic (Final Fantasy VI)|relics]] or equipment pieces, and they are passive during battle. These abilities are not named within the game.

===''[[Final Fantasy VII]]''===
{{See|Support Materia (Final Fantasy VII)|Independent Materia (Final Fantasy VII)}}
Support Materia enhance the linked [[Magic Materia (Final Fantasy VII)|Magic]] or [[Summon Materia (Final Fantasy VII)|Summon Materia]], or use the linked [[Materia (Final Fantasy VII equipment)|Materia's]] status or element to enhance the [[Final Fantasy VII weapons|weapon]] or [[Final Fantasy VII armor|armor]] the linked Materia pair is equipped in. For example, linking [[All (Final Fantasy VII)|All Materia]] to a Magic Materia will have that Materia's spells hit all targets, enemies or allies, but will have no effect on spells that are naturally [[Group-cast|multi-target]].

Independent Materia provide their effects by simply being equipped, and provide stat boosts and other various enhancements, such as making all of the user's abilities target all targets with [[Mega All]].

Some equipment also have support effects. [[Final Fantasy VII accessories|Accessories]] provide various support effects, and some weapons and armor have the innate effect of [[AP bonus abilities|doubling or even tripling]] Materia growth.

====''[[Final Fantasy VII Remake]]''====
{{Main|Support Materia (VII Remake)|Complete Materia (VII Remake)}}
Pairing support materia with {{icon|ffviir|materia|magic}} can be done for various affect, such as using the [[Magnify Materia (VII Remake)|magnify materia]] to apply a spell to all enemies/allies, or to use the [[AP Up Materia (VII Remake)|AP up materia]] to level up another materia piece faster. Complete materia apply their effects automatically by simply equipping them on a character, such as basic stat boosts, or the [[Auto-Cure Materia|auto-cure materia]] that allows the user to automatically use {{icon|FFVIIR|spell|cure}} on an ally in critical health.

====''[[Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-]]''====
{{See|Support materia (Crisis Core)|Special materia}}
[[Zack (Crisis Core player character)|Zack]] can gain various support effects from equipped Materia. Via [[Materia Fusion]], he can also apply bonus effects to Materia. He can also equip various [[Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII- accessories|accessories]] with various supports effects.

===''[[Final Fantasy VIII]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy VIII support abilities}}
Support abilities are learned by [[Guardian Forces]] and equipped through them; without a GF the character can only use the [[Attack (command)#Final Fantasy VIII|Attack]] command and [[Limit Break (Final Fantasy VIII)|Limit Breaks]]. A character can equip a maximum of four support abilities at once. The GFs learn abilities by accumulating [[Ability Points#Final Fantasy VIII|AP]] and via [[Final Fantasy VIII items|items]].

===''[[Final Fantasy IX]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy IX support abilities}}
Characters learn support abilities from equipment. They can be equipped from the menu via [[Magic Stone (Final Fantasy IX)|Magic Stones]], which the party members gain as they level up. The party member can equip the support ability from the equipment as soon as they equip the piece, but after permanently learning the ability by accruing AP in battle, they can equip the support ability even without equipping an equipment piece that provides it. Equipping multiple pieces of equipment that provide that ability multiplies the learn rate.

===''[[Final Fantasy X]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy X auto-abilities}}
Auto-abilities are found in [[Final Fantasy X weapons|weapons]] and [[Final Fantasy X armor|armor]], and can be customized onto them with items after the events at [[Guadosalam]] if the equipment piece has empty slots. A piece of equipment can have four auto-abilities at once. [[Final Fantasy X enemies|Enemies]] [[Item drop#Final Fantasy X|drop]] weapons and armor with abilities on them, and they are available in [[Final Fantasy X shops|shops]]. Some equipment dropped by [[superbosses]], the [[Dark Aeon]]s and [[Penance (Final Fantasy X)|Penance]], have a hidden support effect that yields a higher [[critical hit]] rate for the wielder.

====''[[Final Fantasy X-2]]''====
{{Main|Final Fantasy X-2 auto-abilities}}
[[Dressphere]]s learn support abilities, which are in effect whenever the character is in that dressphere. [[Final Fantasy X-2 accessories|Accessories]] provide support effects no matter which dressphere the character equips, and [[Garment Grid]]s can have special effects activate for that battle only when the character moves between nodes.

====''[[Final Fantasy X-2: Last Mission]]''====

===''[[Final Fantasy XII]]''===
{{See|Augments (Final Fantasy XII)|Final Fantasy XII accessories}}
The playable characters can unlock Augments on the [[License Board]] to gain permanent support effects. In the ''Zodiac'' versions, the augments depend on which job the character has.

Equipping accessories also provides various effects, and some equipment also have enhancing effects, such as [[Auto-Shell]] or [[Auto-Protect]].

====''[[Final Fantasy XII: Revenant Wings]]''====
{{Main|Final Fantasy XII: Revenant Wings abilities}}
Characters gain support effects from accessories they can equip. Each playable character has unique equipment.

===''[[Final Fantasy XIII]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy XIII passive abilities}}
There are two types of support abilities: Auto abilities, which are exclusive to the five of six [[paradigm|roles]] (excluding [[Medic (Final Fantasy XIII)|Medic]]), and passive abilities, which are [[Final Fantasy XIII weapons|weapon]] and [[Final Fantasy XIII accessories|accessory]] skills. Equipping multiple equipment pieces in the same synthesis group also unlocks additional effects, like [[Stagger (Final Fantasy XIII)#Random: Instant Chain|Random: Instant Chain]].

====''[[Final Fantasy XIII-2]]''====
{{Main|Final Fantasy XIII-2 passive abilities}}
There are two types of support abilities: Auto abilities, which are exclusive to the five of six roles (excluding [[Medic (Final Fantasy XIII-2)|Medic]]), and passive abilities which are [[Final Fantasy XIII-2 weapons|weapon]] and [[Final Fantasy XIII-2 accessories|accessory]] skills. [[Paradigm Pack]] monsters learn various skills by leveling up in the [[Crystarium system]], and the player can [[Paradigm Pack#Infusion|infuse]] them with other monsters to transfer their learned abilities.

====''[[Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII]]''====
{{Main|Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII auto-abilities}}
The role auto abilities and equipment passive abilities are merged into a single category of auto-abilities. [[Lightning (Lightning Returns party member)|Lightning]] can trigger these support effects via various [[Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII garbs|garbs]], [[Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII weapons|weapons]], [[Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII shields|shields]] and [[Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII accessories|accessories]].

===''[[Final Fantasy XIV]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy XIV traits}}

===''[[Final Fantasy XV]]''===
{{Main|Ascension (Final Fantasy XV)}}
The player can unlock new support abilities from the Ascension grid, where the effects are learned permanently. The player can also get various effects from [[Final Fantasy XV accessories|accessories]] and [[attire]]s, and some [[Final Fantasy XV weapons|weapons]] have special effects.

===''[[Final Fantasy Tactics]]''===
{{Main|Final Fantasy Tactics support abilities}}
Support abilities are learned by [[Final Fantasy Tactics jobs|jobs]] or tied to equipment.
